clue.text: Traitor steals horse from one's carriage

parts.note: one is I, so one's gives I'S

indicators.note: a thief steals a thing from somewhere, so the letter for horse is lifted out of the phrase

parts.note: a chariot is a horse-drawn carriage
H is slang for heroin, known as horse

explanation.surface: A traitor makes off with a horse taken from someone's carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking H out of I'S CHARIOT leaves the traitor's name. 'Horse' is drug slang for heroin, abbreviated H.
explanation.definitionFit: Judas Iscariot betrayed Jesus, and his surname became a byword for a betrayer.

clue.text: Round range, following track is not free

indicators.note: round placed before the pieces asks for the track to go around them

parts.note: a spoor is the trail or track left by an animal
ken is range of knowledge or sight
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: A hunter's circuit of the range along a track means the land is reserved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' looks like the definition or a ring, but it is the container signal; a spoor is a hunter's term for an animal's trail.
explanation.definitionFit: Something already claimed or reserved is spoken for, so is not available.

clue.text: Worried about famous actress, a goddess

indicators.note: about means the word for worried is placed around the actress

parts.note: ate, as in 'what's eating you?', means worried or troubled
a famous actress is a star

explanation.surface: Someone frets over a celebrated actress who is treated like a goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worried' looks like an anagram signal, but it means troubled, as in 'what's eating you?'.
explanation.definitionFit: Astarte was the Phoenician goddess of fertility and love.

clue.text: Johnson's work comparatively shoddy?

definitions.meaning: a series of essays by Samuel Johnson published in the eighteenth century
more idle, that is lazier or less worked on, so of poorer quality

explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Johnson wrote a series of essays under the title The Idler; the question mark flags the loose second sense of idle as poorly done.
explanation.definitionFit: The Idler was Johnson's essay series, and the comparative of idle describes something done with even less effort.

clue.text: Head over to beer barrel

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: Someone heads over to the beer barrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' reverses NUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tun is a large cask, especially for beer or wine.

clue.text: Astrologer pins down Marquis

indicators.note: pins means holds fast inside, so the astrologer encloses the word for down

parts.note: John Dee was the astrologer to Elizabeth I
down means low in spirits, sad

explanation.surface: A stargazer pins down an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pins down' reads as one phrase, but 'down' is fodder meaning unhappy. Dee was Elizabeth I's astrologer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Marquis de Sade was the French aristocrat and writer who gave his name to sadism.

clue.text: Beaten down daughter rose to succeed amazingly

indicators.note: beaten means knocked about, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A beaten, dejected daughter recovered and went on to remarkable success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beaten' rearranges DOWN, D and ROSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To do wonders is an idiom for achieving remarkable results.

clue.text: Site of castle perhaps with strip of land outside

indicators.note: outside means the strip of land is put around the word for with

parts.note: a spit is a narrow point of land running into the sea
and means with, together with

explanation.surface: A castle stands on a narrow strip of land with water around it.
explanation.walkthrough: The castle is a sandcastle: 'perhaps' warns it is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Children build sandcastles in a pit of sand, so it is one place a castle might be found.

clue.text: Think vaguely about interrupting beaver's work

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so the word for about goes inside

parts.note: beavers build dams
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone muses idly about interrupting a beaver building.
explanation.definitionFit: To dream is to let the mind wander in vague, idle thought.

clue.text: Item for sale around fine room

indicators.note: around means the item for sale goes about the letter for fine

parts.note: a lot is an item put up at auction
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An auction item sits around a fine room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' puts LOT about F.
explanation.definitionFit: A loft is a room or space under the roof of a house.

clue.text: Interminable ache, child's wound perhaps

parts.note: to ache for is to long for
a child might wrongly form the past tense of wind as winded instead of wound

explanation.surface: An endless ache from a child's wound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound' is not an injury but the past of wind, which a child might say as 'winded'; 'perhaps' marks that playful guess.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-winded speech goes on and on, so it seems interminable.

clue.text: Herod had head removed and put in dish, according to poet

indicators.note: put in means the trimmed word is placed inside the dish

parts.note: a pan is a cooking dish

indicators.note: had head removed means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: Herod Antipas was the tetrarch of Galilee

explanation.surface: Herod had someone beheaded and the head served on a dish, as a poet tells it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls John the Baptist's head on a platter. Herod is not fodder: his title is what loses its head, its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Petrarchan means in the style of the Italian poet Petrarch, as in the Petrarchan sonnet.

clue.text: Shortly considered religious work to be peak of inspiration

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, losing the word's final letter

parts.note: held means considered, as in held to be true
an icon is a religious painting

explanation.surface: A brief look at a devotional painting leads to a summit of inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' trims HELD to HEL. Mount Helicon in Greece was sacred to the Muses.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Helicon was home to the Muses, so it stands for the source of poetic inspiration.

clue.text: Cat a foolish person without pet rejected

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the whole assembled run is read backwards
without means the word for pet is taken away

parts.note: a muppet is slang for a foolish person
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cat turns away a fool who has no pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' turns the whole run, A included, after the pet is removed from the fool; 'muppet' is British slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: The puma is a large American wild cat, also called the cougar.

clue.text: Post a couple of lines anyway

parts.note: post as a prefix means after
L is line, so two of them give LL

explanation.surface: Send a couple of lines in the mail regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' looks like a verb about mailing but means after, as in post-war.
explanation.definitionFit: After all is an idiom meaning in any case or nevertheless.

clue.text: Positive set varies unpredictably

indicators.note: unpredictably means in no fixed order, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A firm set of results varies unpredictably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unpredictably' rearranges SET and VARIES.
explanation.definitionFit: An assertive person is confident and positive in stating views.

clue.text: Cause fowl to lose head, and other end

indicators.note: to lose head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: a hen is a domestic fowl
the tail is the end opposite the head

explanation.surface: Make a chicken lose its head and its tail too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cause' is a verb here: to entail is to bring about.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail is to involve or bring about as a consequence, so to cause.

clue.text: Combine to fell giant tree

indicators.note: fell means cut down, so the letters of the tree are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Teams join forces to fell an enormous tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell' rearranges GIANT TREE.
explanation.definitionFit: To integrate is to combine parts into a whole.

clue.text: Plant occurs in the wild

indicators.note: in the wild means running free, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A plant that grows in the wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the wild' rearranges OCCURS.
explanation.definitionFit: The crocus is a small flowering plant grown from a corm.

clue.text: From island, dismiss Russian

parts.note: Cos, or Kos, is a Greek island
to sack is to dismiss from a job

explanation.surface: A Russian is dismissed from an island.
explanation.walkthrough: COS is the Greek island also spelt Kos.
explanation.definitionFit: Cossacks are a people of southern Russia and Ukraine famed as horsemen.

clue.text: Result of random extremes of thuggery?

definitions.text: Result of random extremes of thuggery?

parts.note: casual means random or chance

indicators.note: extremes of picks the first and last letters of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone injured by an act of random violence.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a victim is what random thuggery produces.
explanation.definitionFit: A casualty is a person hurt in an accident or attack, as random violence would produce.

clue.text: Excitement of a short part in play touring the States

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the shortened part encloses the States
short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a role is an actor's part in a play
USA stands for the United States of America

explanation.surface: The thrill of a small part in a play touring America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' trims the stage part by its last letter, and 'touring' wraps it around the country's three-letter abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Arousal is a state of excitement or stimulation.

clue.text: Advantage to make sign of the cross

definitions.meaning: a benefit or point in favour
the arithmetic symbol for addition is a small upright cross

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign of the cross' is not the religious gesture but the addition sign, which is a cross.
explanation.definitionFit: A plus is an advantage, and the addition symbol is a cross.

clue.text: Call an ornament a bit plain

indicators.note: a bit means only part of the phrase is used, a run of letters inside it

explanation.surface: Calling an ornament a bit plain.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'caLL AN Ornament'.
explanation.definitionFit: A llano is a grassy treeless plain in South America.

clue.text: Spend very little time in practice?

definitions.meaning: to pass quickly through a place without stopping
a rehearsal of a performance from start to finish

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the noun sense: a rehearsal is a practice of the whole piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To go rapidly through somewhere is one sense, and a rehearsal is another.

clue.text: Using sound, cures parts of body

indicators.note: using sound means the word is spoken, so a word that sounds the same is entered

parts.note: to heal is to cure

explanation.surface: Sound treatment cures parts of the body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Using sound' looks like a medical method but signals a word that sounds like HEALS.
explanation.definitionFit: The heels are the back parts of the feet.

clue.text: A language employed by head in princely land

indicators.note: employed by means taken in by, so the head holds the other pieces

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
Latin is a classical language

explanation.surface: A language used by the head of a princely realm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Employed by' signals containment: the head takes in the language. Pate is an old word for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A palatinate is a territory ruled by a count palatine or prince, such as the German Palatinate.

clue.text: Always first to reach port

parts.note: ay or aye is an old word for always

indicators.note: first to picks out the initial letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Always the first ship to reach port.
explanation.walkthrough: AY is the archaic word for ever; AYR is a port on Scotland's west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayr is a Scottish harbour town on the Firth of Clyde.

clue.text: Hands back the exchange

indicators.note: back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: paws is informal for hands

explanation.surface: Hands go back across the exchange counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reverses PAWS.
explanation.definitionFit: To swap is to exchange one thing for another.

clue.text: Piece of computer data that's taken to falsify

indicators.note: taken to means attached at the end, so the second piece follows the first

parts.note: to cook the books is to falsify accounts
i.e. is short for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Computer data that is used to fake records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' means falsify, as in cooking the books; i.e. stands for 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cookie is a small file a website stores on a user's computer.

clue.text: Mended shoes holding very firm

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the mended shoes surround the letter for very

parts.note: resoled shoes have had new soles fitted

explanation.surface: Repaired shoes are held to be very firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holding' puts V inside RESOLED.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolved means determined, firm in purpose.
